first_frame: Cinematic 16:9 military-documentary film still, the opening frame of a documentary. Night on flat, cold Yellow Sea water under a dark overcast sky: a grey South Korean Pohang-class corvette - a low, sleek 88-metre hull, one small gun on the foredeck, a single lattice mast, no lights on - cruises from left to right in the middle distance, seen side-on from wave height. Faint cold moonlight through thin cloud edges the grey hull and the gentle swell; the ship is fully visible from bow to stern with open dark water ahead of it. No hull numbers, no names, no flags with readable text. Photorealistic simulated-footage military-documentary recreation, never cartoon. Subtle film grain, restrained cinematic grade, crushed blacks, natural light falloff. ONE SINGLE FULL-FRAME 16:9 PHOTOGRAPH - not a grid, collage, contact sheet or split-screen. The photograph fills the entire 16:9 frame edge to edge with NO black bars, NO letterboxing, NO pillarboxing, no border and no matte of any kind. No inset picture, no picture-in-picture panel, no camera HUD, no REC indicator, no timestamp. No text, letters, words, subtitles or captions anywhere in frame. No people visible.
